description: Default capability: the app's own webview may invoke the engine-bridge commands, and nothing else. Matched on `webviews: ["main"]`, NOT `windows: ["main"]` — the main window now hosts untrusted child webviews (browser-*) alongside the UI's own, and a child reports its parent's window label; a window-matched grant would be inherited by every page seated in the window and hand the whole `codify_*` surface to untrusted content. The `shell` permission set (src-tauri/permissions/shell.json) is this app's ACL manifest — before it existed, Tauri let a *local*-origin invoke of any `codify_*` command through with no capability check at all, which is the bypass this capability also closes. It names the sixteen commands one by one rather than granting a wildcard. No shell or filesystem scope is granted: the frontend only uses `invoke`, and the engine is spawned by the Rust backend over tokio, not through the shell plugin.
